payload.claim: Criterion 1's claim includes "...the push is a fast-forward..." as part of the single sentence its witness must drive, but RoutedRecord.append/RefsRecord.append never push on their own (push is the separate RoutedRecord.push/RefsRecord.push path, confirmed by reading routed.py and by running a prototype of the change — the origin's refs were untouched after an append). So for that clause of the claim to actually be exercised, the witness must itself call .push() after the append and check the remote accepts it as a fast-forward; it is not something the append path demonstrates by itself. This is implicit in "Each runs against a real bare origin under tmp_path" and is a procedural detail for whoever writes the test, not a defect in the criterion, but it is worth flagging so it isn't accidentally dropped when the witness is written.
